reviews.title: Powerhouse Performance for Gamers and Creators! ⚡🖥️
reviews.comment: The Intel® Core™ i7-11700KF is an absolute beast of a processor, and it’s been the perfect choice for my high-performance PC build. With 8 cores and a turbo boost of up to 5.0 GHz, it handles everything I throw at it, from intense gaming sessions to video editing and multitasking, without breaking a sweat. Since it’s unlocked, overclocking is a breeze for squeezing out even more performance, and paired with a good cooling solution, it stays cool and stable. This CPU also takes full advantage of PCIe 4.0, making it perfect for high-speed SSDs and GPUs. I love that it skips the integrated graphics, allowing me to focus entirely on my discrete GPU. It’s an excellent choice for gamers who want raw power and for creators who need smooth performance for demanding applications. If you’re building a PC and want a processor that delivers top-tier performance at a great value, the i7-11700KF is a no-brainer. Highly recommend it for anyone looking to take their setup to the next level! 🚀✨

reviews.title: The Best Line
reviews.comment: The Intel line is the best and most stable processor made. Just place it in its socket and boot and you'll be up and running - whether it be i5, i7, or i9.
reviews.author: RFM

reviews.title: So far so good.
reviews.comment: Working great so far, was a much needed upgrade from my i5-4670k..I jumped from 2012 to 2022 in one grand leap of upgrades, into "oh wow my CPU isn't at 100% when playing these games anymore?" (GTA V, Tarkov, FiveM, etc.) Running in this setup: MSI Z590 motherboard, 64gb Corsair Vengeance RAM (2x 32gb), Gigabyte RTX 3060 Gaming OC, Evga Supernova 750 G6 power supply, and the Noctua NH-U12S Redux as the CPU cooler keeps this going just fine. Everything air cooled since the last cooler was a liquid cooler that spontaneously screwed me over one day when the pumps failed while I was out of the house (somehow didn't fry anything besides my nerves). Watching the temperature on the CPU with this cooler, I have rarely seen the CPU hit 67c while running TWO instances of GTA V on max graphics.
